label: June 2026 paper — gap-fill practice variants (booklet Q1–Q50)

items.stem: 10 items with exponential lifetimes of mean θ are put on test, and the test stops at the fourth failure. The failure times are 2, 3, 5, 6. The unbiased estimate of θ based on the first r = 4 order statistics is
items.explanation: For type II censoring the total time on test is Σᵢ₌₁ʳ X₍ᵢ₎ + (n − r)X₍ᵣ₎: the r failures plus the n − r survivors, each observed up to X₍ᵣ₎. It is θ times a Gamma(r, 1) variable, so dividing by r gives an unbiased estimator: (16 + 6 × 6)/4 = 13. Trap: the plain average of the failure times ignores the 6 survivors and underestimates θ.

items.stem: Two independent groups give scores ES: 65, 57, 74, 43, 39 and LC: 85, 87, 72, 98, 90. The Mann–Whitney U statistic (the smaller of U_ES and U_LC) is
items.explanation: U_ES counts the pairs in which an ES score beats an LC score: only 74 beats 72, so U_ES = 1, and U_LC = 5 × 5 − 1 = 24. The statistic is the smaller, 1. Trap: U_ES + U_LC = n₁n₂ = 25, so the larger value 24 is just the complement.
